simulation.note: behavioural switch and logic model; this is not a device model, not a thermal model, and not a hardware measurement

pmos_selection.reason: no P-channel MOSFET datasheet in references/datasheets; external acquisition is blocked in this environment, and a fabricated orderable code is worse than an empty one

requirements.body_diode: standard P-MOS body diode, drain-to-source; the common-drain pair must present opposing diodes

why.vds: 15 V rail plus back-fed VDD_SR; 30 V gives 2x margin
why.id_pulsed: C54 (3.3 uF) charges through the switch at turn-on; the supply and wiring set the peak, so the part must have pulsed headroom. No soft-start is fitted.
why.ciss: R50 turn-off is 100k * Ciss; at 100 pF the gate crosses Vth in ~14 us, after the ~12 us crowbar has already crossed REG UVLO
why.rds_on: the SR bias is ~15 mA; 0.1 ohm is 1.5 mV, not a thermal constraint, but keeps the pass drop negligible
why.vgs_th: Q55 is a source follower driven by VDD_IN; it can only lift the gate when the back-fed VDD_SR exceeds VDD_IN by more than |Vth|. With a 3 V backfeed the part has to be a logic-level P-MOS, |Vth| <= 2.5 V at the quoted test current, or Q51 stays partly on

pmos_selection.not_acceptable: BSS84-class parts are not automatically acceptable: no datasheet is held, and the 3.3 uF turn-on pulse is outside a small-signal default assumption.

cut_points.VDD_IN: existing SR board VDD_IN, after D2 (SS34)
cut_points.VDD_SR: existing SR board VDD node; JP1 stays between VDD_SR and VDD as a service disconnect, not as the protection
cut_points.FAULT_G: existing R40/R41/C40 node, shared with the Q41/R44 crowbar

integration.preserved_fast_path: Q41 + R44 remain directly driven by FAULT_G. This module does not include, bypass, or delay them.
integration.five_volt_source: J7 must be fed from a 5 V rail that survives the SR bias cut. If that rail is lost, the P-MOS gate is pulled to VDD_IN by R50, so the bias is removed (fail-safe), but the latch is also unpowered.

observations.finding: R50 pulls BC_GATE to VDD_IN, R52 pulls ENABLE low, and R60 pulls PERMIT low. A floating or unpowered control domain leaves the switch off.
SET = FLT_H OR POR is evaluated before RST_EFF; a fault that is still present cannot be cleared by RESET_CMD.
when SET and RST_EFF are both false the latch holds. A fault that disappears does not restore the bias.
observations.evidence: truth_table rows with fault=False, por=False, reset=False

observations.finding: Q50/Q51 share a drain (VMID) so their body diodes oppose. With the switch off, neither body diode conducts from VDD_IN or VDD_SR into VMID. Q55 + D50 pull the gate up with VDD_SR when VDD_SR is back-fed above VDD_IN, and D50 also blocks Q55's body diode in the off state. Residual: VDD_SR -> Q55 -> D50 -> R50 -> VDD_IN is ~30 uA at VDD_SR=18 V; it is a bleed in the safe direction, not switch conduction.
when ENABLE is low, ENABLE_N is high and Q54+R57 discharge VDD_SR; R58 is the passive bleed if the 5 V domain is lost. 47 ohm * 3.3 uF is 155 us, ~220 us to 3.63 V.

R61 pulls FAULT_G low, so a disconnected fault source reads as no-fault. This is the existing fail-open input policy and is deliberately opposite to the fail-safe bias cut; they are different circuits, see docs/2026-11-06_REG保持热边界与偏置关断审核.md section 4.

the crowbar crosses REG UVLO in ~12.11 us (existing estimate); the 5 V logic adds <1 us; the gate network adds ~14 us; the local discharge adds ~220 us. The crowbar is the fast path, the bias cut is the long-hold path.
observations.evidence: arithmetic; the gate time uses an assumed 60 pF Ciss

observations.finding: no hardware, no thermal sign-off, no measured reverse backfeed into VDD/REG, no SOA for the P-MOS turn-on pulse.
